target_only_tests.note: Five groups, none counted as ported coverage. (1) Seven pin the two inherited defects REPAIRED in this pass under D-0023 -- the malformed-`filesystem` coercion (D-0215) and the case-sensitive `_is_inside_root` (D-0216) -- each with the half it must not break beside it: every falsy `filesystem` still renders as the source renders it, a disabled sandbox is still not refused, the reported read roots still carry the operator's spelling, and POSIX identity stays case-SENSITIVE. Both repairs were MEASURED before and after rather than reasoned about; the numbers are in `intentional_divergences`. (2) Two pin D-0211's number-spelling obligation at this module's one container rebuild, `findingToJsonable`, which moves a number from a deny array's numeric index onto the key `source` -- so the wholesale `carryNumberSpellings` matches nothing and silently does nothing. A spelling cannot be written in TypeScript, so both build the document as TEXT, read it back through the production path and assert on the serialiser's output. (3) One is rule 5's seam-liveness obligation for `doctorSeams`, covering all five keys. (4) Three pin `shutil.which`, added by the review gate's round 2. The first draft split `PATH` and skipped empty components, which loses three CPython behaviours in the SAME direction: an unset `PATH` falls back to `os.defpath` where an empty one searches nowhere; an empty component searches the current directory; and directories are deduplicated by their normcased form. Each lost one makes the lookup answer `null` for a `bwrap` that is in fact reachable, and this module answers a failed lookup with `CANARY_SKIPPED` -- which, with no static findings, exits 0. A preflight reporting success without running its live check is the silent pass the command exists to prevent. Every value was measured against CPython 3.12.3 rather than read off `shutil.py`. One thing these cases do NOT pin, recorded because the probe said so and the first draft's comment claimed otherwise: swapping `osJoin` for `node:path`'s `join` leaves them green -- both turn an empty first component into the bare name, and they differ only in a normalisation no `stat` can observe. (5) Four pin the two argparse actions this CLI needed and `src/settings/argparse.ts` did not have (`append`, `store_false`). Each of the fourteen was probed by reverting the code it pins and confirming it goes red for its own stated reason (`docs/test-translation-conventions.md` section 10). That probe is what corrected one of them: the store_false-default case does NOT fire when `defaultValue: true` is deleted from the spec in `cli.ts`, because `spec.defaultValue ?? true` supplies it -- which is CPython's own redundancy, and is now written into the case rather than assumed.

approved_non_running.reason: The source's two capability gates, `@requires_symlinks` and `@requires_bwrap`, each spelled as ONE `skipIf` bound to a module-level constant and reused by every case that needs it -- 42 and 2 cases respectively -- rather than as one `skipIf` per case. Both conditions are PROBED at module load (collection time, as pytest's `skipif` is) rather than inferred from `process.platform`, and the source says why for each: Windows creates symlinks under Developer Mode or elevation, so a blanket `skipif(win32)` would give up coverage on hosts that can run these; and bwrap's presence is not its ability to start, because Ubuntu 24.04 and many containers block the unprivileged user namespaces it needs. Both ran on the porting host and both run on this repository's Ubuntu cells. The `escaping_home` fixture's own `pytest.skip` is the first of the two, reached through the same constant.

entries.reason: The source simulates ntpath by `monkeypatch.setattr(generator.os, 'path', ntpath)` plus `os.sep` and `os.altsep`. This port has no `os` module object to patch: `src/fencing/pypath.ts` transcribes both namespaces and dispatches on `process.platform` at CALL time (D-0200, D-0213), so the same simulation is a `process.platform` of `"win32"` for the length of the case, installed with `Object.defineProperty` because `platform` is a getter and a silently ignored assignment would leave the case running on POSIX and passing for the wrong reason. Same three answers changed, same injected `islink_fn` / `readlink_fn`, and every assertion is the source's -- including the two that name the drive-relative bug's signature.

entries.reason: The source asserts the ASCII policy by encoding to cp932 and letting `UnicodeEncodeError` fail the case. JavaScript has no cp932 encoder and needs none: ASCII is a strict subset of cp932, so `isAscii` implies the source's assertion rather than weakening it. Both of the source's two subjects are checked -- the verbose report and the parser's help text -- and the help text is `buildDoctorParser().help()`, this port's `build_parser().format_help()`.

intentional_divergences.topic: An enabled sandbox whose `filesystem` is a truthy NON-mapping is REFUSED rather than coerced to `{}` (D-0215).
intentional_divergences.source_behaviour: `settings/generator.py` `_evaluate_sandbox_suppressions` is `fs = sandbox.get('filesystem') or {}` followed by `if not isinstance(fs, dict): fs = {}`. Measured on this port before the repair: a role declaring `sandbox: {enabled: true, filesystem: "invalid"}` renders `{"enabled":true,"filesystem":{"denyRead":[],"denyWrite":[]}}` -- a malformed security configuration silently becoming a valid, less restrictive one.
intentional_divergences.port_behaviour: `PyValueError: sandbox.filesystem must be an object, got str: 'invalid'`, which `run` turns into `error: ...` and rc 2. Only a TRUTHY non-mapping raises: `pyOr` has already replaced an absent, `null`, `{}`, `[]`, `0` or `""` `filesystem` with `{}` before the check, so every document interlock accepts is still accepted (pinned, six rows). The refusal sits after the `enabled` gate, exactly where the coercion sat, so a disabled sandbox is unaffected (pinned).
intentional_divergences.why_here: This one was escalated to PR 4 by PR #43's review gate specifically because the READBACK is what observes it, and PR 4 owns the readback. Measured: `sandbox doctor`, handed the pre-repair render, reports `deny targets: 0 (0 unusable by bwrap)` and `RESULT: sandbox deny paths are usable by bwrap.` A clean bill of health for a file whose author's `filesystem` key was thrown away -- and a preflight that gates a launch, per its own module note, `must not pass by accident`. The warrant for the repair is that interlock ALREADY refuses this shape one module over: `sandbox_doctor.validate_settings` answers a non-mapping `sandbox.filesystem` with `sandbox.filesystem must be an object` and exits 2. The generator writing the file and the doctor checking it disagreed about the same shape; the message here is the doctor's own sentence so that they no longer do, and that agreement is asserted rather than left as a resemblance.
intentional_divergences.platforms: EVERY platform, unlike D-0213's `os.path.isabs` repair -- interlock renders `denyRead: []` for this input on Linux too. That difference is why the disclosure said this one needed a decision id of its own.

intentional_divergences.topic: `_is_inside_root` compares normcased paths, so a Windows drive-letter case difference is not a sandbox escape (D-0216).
intentional_divergences.source_behaviour: `settings/generator.py` `_is_inside_root` compares with `==` and `startswith`, both case-SENSITIVE, and applies `os.path.normcase` on neither side. Measured on this port before the repair, under a simulated ntpath: a `worker_dir` authored `c:\Users\Foo\worker` against a realpath returned as `C:\Users\Foo\worker\secret` renders `denyRead: []` with one suppression whose reason is `realpath escapes sandbox read roots`. The two paths name the same directory, and the dropped entry is an in-root deny -- the kind that covers a credential file inside the worker directory.
intentional_divergences.port_behaviour: The COMPARISON is normcased and nothing else. `osNormcase` is CPython's `ntpath.normcase` / `posixpath.normcase` pair, added to `src/fencing/pypath.ts` and checked against CPython 3.12.3 by `parity/oracle/ospath-vector.json` as a seventh function, on every matrix cell. After the repair the same input keeps the entry and suppresses nothing.
intentional_divergences.why_here: The disclosure said this one needed a DESIGN call rather than a substitution, and named it: whether `sandbox_read_roots` REPORTS the normcased form or the operator's. Answered by scoping the fold to the comparison. `metadata.sandboxReadRoots` is what `settings show --explain` prints and what the launcher's /sandbox status displays, and an operator has to recognise the path they wrote; normcasing the stored roots would have folded a display value to answer a comparison question. Both halves are pinned, and the display half would stay green under the wrong answer to the other, which is why it is its own case.
intentional_divergences.platforms: Windows only. `posixpath.normcase` is the identity, so this is a no-op on the platform interlock runs on -- but unlike D-0213's `isabs` repair that is a property of the PLATFORM rather than of the substitution, so it is recorded as a deliberate divergence and pinned in the direction that would break: two paths differing only in case are two different files on POSIX, and an entry under one must still not be judged in-root by the other.

inherited_limitations.what: `collect_deny_targets` reads `permissions.deny` and the two Layer 3 arrays but not `permissions.ask`, and not the `additionalDirectories` that widen the sandbox rather than narrowing it. A scope that contributes an unbindable path through a key this list does not name is not audited, and the report says `deny targets: N` without saying which keys N was drawn from.
inherited_limitations.source: settings/sandbox_doctor.py `collect_deny_targets` -- the two layers are transcribed verbatim, including the docstring's reason for collecting both.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: Upstream, and only with evidence. The two layers are the ones Claude Code's sandboxing documentation names as merging into the bwrap deny set; adding a third on the strength of a reading would widen a security check by guess, which is rule 11's shape. The live canary is the compensating control: it binds what was collected and reports whether the sandbox actually comes up.

inherited_limitations.what: The bwrap canary binds only paths that already exist (`os.path.lexists`), so a deny path naming a file that has not been created yet is skipped by the live half and judged by the static half alone. A path that would be unbindable for a reason other than a symlink goes unreported until the file exists.
inherited_limitations.source: settings/sandbox_doctor.py `run_bwrap_canary`: `if literal is None or not os.path.lexists(literal): continue` -- transcribed verbatim.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: Neither side. Binding a non-existent source is what bwrap itself refuses, so probing one would report a failure of the probe rather than of the settings -- the canary would fail every run that denied a not-yet-created credential file, and an operator who learned to ignore it would be ignoring the real ones too. The residual is disclosed rather than fixed because the alternative is a check nobody reads.

inherited_limitations.what: `discover_merged_scopes` names `~/.claude/settings.json` and two managed-settings paths, and derives project scopes from each input's directory. Claude Code's enterprise and policy scopes on other platforms -- and any scope an operator adds by configuration -- are not discovered, so `--no-merge-scopes` and the default differ by a fixed list rather than by what the client will actually merge.
inherited_limitations.source: settings/sandbox_doctor.py `USER_SETTINGS_PATH`, `MANAGED_SETTINGS_PATHS`, `PROJECT_SCOPE_FILENAMES` and `discover_merged_scopes` -- transcribed verbatim, list included.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: Upstream, tracked against the client's documented scope list. The port keeps the list rather than extending it: a scope added here and not there would make the two implementations disagree about what a clean preflight means, and the command's whole value is that its answer matches the launch.
